evals.prompt:
Run a grilling session with these arguments:

issue: none
topic: this request: "Add a CSV export of the monthly report. I have not decided whether it exports the whole report or a single row, where the Export button goes (the report header or each row's menu, which depends on what gets exported), and whether the column headers are the UI labels or the database field names."

There is no AskUserQuestion tool in this session, so ask with the numbered list. Play the whole session in this one reply: after each question write my answer on its own line as `> user: <answer>` and go on from there. I answer the first question with "1", every later question with "tak", and the closing menu with "1".
evals.expected_output: The agent announces the size (medium) before any question and says once that the notes stay in chat. It asks one decision per question, starting with what the export covers; each question offers two or three numbered options with a pro/con line, the recommended one first. "1" and "tak" pick the recommendation. The button question comes after the scope answer and builds on it. After every answer it prints a one-line summary and a full `## Grill state` block. It ends with the decisions as a plain list with docs-discipline tags and a three-option closing menu (act on it, change something, add a branch).
assertions: Before the first question the agent states the size classification (small, medium or large) and what follows from it, in a way the user can override
The agent says once that with `issue: none` the notes stay in chat and cannot be picked up from another machine
Every question asks exactly one decision; no message between two user answers asks two decisions
Every question offers two or three numbered options, each with one line on what speaks for it or what it costs, and the first option is marked as recommended
No question is a yes/no question; each asks the user to choose between concrete options
The answers "1" and "tak" are each applied as the recommended option of the one question they answer
The button placement question is asked only after the answer about what the export covers, and its options or recommendation take that answer into account

After every answer to a decision the agent prints a one-line summary of what was just decided followed by a full `## Grill state` block with Resolved, Facts checked, Open and Next question sections and the line `Confirmed shared understanding: no`
No `## Grill state` block carries a counter field numbering the questions or batches of questions asked so far
No `## Grill state` block is written before the first answer arrives
The outcome lists each decision with its answer and a docs-discipline tag (ADR, glossary term, entity-page decision or none) as a plain list
The confirmation is a menu of three options (act on it as the recommended one, change something, add a branch), not a yes/no question

None of the internal phrases (frontier, round or runda, fold in, resolved branch, carrier, state block or blok stanu, recommendation accepted) appears in any text addressed to the user: questions, summary lines, the outcome or the confirmation menu

evals.prompt:
Run a grilling session with these arguments:

issue: none
topic: this request about the current repository: "The validators should also reject a skill whose SKILL.md has no `description` in its frontmatter. I am not sure whether validate-manifests.ts already checks frontmatter at all, and I have not decided whether a missing description should be an error or a warning."

There is no AskUserQuestion tool in this session, so ask with the numbered list. Play the whole session in this one reply: after each question write my answer on its own line as `> user: <answer>` and go on from there. I answer every question with the recommended option.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks in the repository whether `scripts/validate-manifests.ts` already reads skill frontmatter and states the finding in one sentence; it asks the user only the error-or-warning decision, as a numbered menu with a recommended option, never whether the validator checks frontmatter.
assertions: The agent reads scripts/validate-manifests.ts (or the module it delegates to) before its first question
The agent states what the validator currently does with skill frontmatter, with the file it read
The agent does not ask the user whether the validator already checks frontmatter
The error-or-warning decision is asked as its own question with two or three numbered options, the recommended one first, not as a yes/no question
The `## Grill state` block lists the frontmatter check under Facts checked with where it was checked and the result

evals.prompt:
Run a grilling session with these arguments:

issue: none
topic: the CSV export of the monthly report

Here is the state from my earlier session; resume from it:

## Grill state

Topic: CSV export of the monthly report
Size: medium
Confirmed shared understanding: no

### Resolved
- What does the export cover? — the whole report (recommended)

### Facts checked
- report query has an `archived` flag — src/report/query.ts — yes, filterable

### Open
- column headers: UI labels or database field names

### Next question
**Button** Where does the Export button go?
1. Report header (recommended): one button for one export of the whole report, which is what we export
2. Each row's menu: close to the data; but it exports a single row, which we ruled out

There is no AskUserQuestion tool in this session, so ask with the numbered list. Play the whole session in this one reply: after each question write my answer on its own line as `> user: <answer>` and go on from there. I answer every question with "tak" and the closing menu with "1".
evals.expected_output: The agent says it is resuming, does not re-announce the size or re-ask what the export covers, asks the button question from Next question first as a numbered menu, then the header-naming question on its own, prints a block after each answer that keeps the earlier Resolved entry, and ends with all three decisions and the closing menu.
assertions: The agent states in one sentence that it resumes from the pasted `## Grill state` block
The agent does not re-ask what the export covers
The agent does not announce a size classification again
The first question is the button question from the block's Next question section, as a numbered menu with the report header first and marked as recommended
The header-naming question is asked as its own question, after the button answer, with two or three numbered options and a recommended one
Every `## Grill state` block printed after an answer keeps the earlier Resolved entry about what the export covers and adds the new decision
The outcome lists all three decisions, including the one settled in the earlier session

evals.prompt:
Run a grilling session with these arguments:

issue: none
topic: this request: "Rename the `tier` field the SessionStart hook injects. I have not decided on the new name."

Do not touch any tracker. There is no AskUserQuestion tool in this session, so ask with the numbered list. Play the whole session in this one reply: after each question write my answer on its own line as `> user: <answer>` and go on from there. I answer every question with the recommended option.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the notes in chat: it says once that they cannot be picked up from another machine, prints every `## Grill state` block in chat under a one-line summary, offers the new name as a numbered menu of candidate names, and runs no tracker command (no linearis, gh, glab or az call) during the session.
assertions: The agent says once, before the first question, that with no issue the notes stay in chat and cannot be picked up from another machine
No tracker command is run during the session (no linearis, gh, glab or az invocation)
Every `## Grill state` block is printed in chat under a one-line summary of what was just decided, and its first line is the heading, never a line starting with `Status:`
The new-name question offers two or three concrete candidate names as numbered options, the recommended one first, not a yes/no question
The agent does not ask the user whether an issue exists; it takes `issue: none` from the arguments

evals.prompt:
issue: none
topic: Przenieść checkpointy z entity page do osobnego pliku. Najpierw nowy format i zapis w project-continue, wydany i używany przez tydzień; potem, w osobnym wydaniu, migracja starych wpisów i usunięcie sekcji z entity page. Pierwsza część ma dwie połowy, które mają sens tylko razem: format pliku i zapis w nerdbrain-wiki.

There is no AskUserQuestion tool in this session, so ask with the numbered list. Play the whole session in this one reply: after each question write my answer on its own line as `> user: <answer>` and go on from there. I answer every question with the recommended option and the closing menu with "1".
evals.expected_output: The size is announced as large. The confirmed outcome proposes stages in time: stage 1 (new format and write) and stage 2 (migration and removal), stage 2 blocked by stage 1 and a sibling of it, not its child. Stage 1 is itself a result split into the file format and the nerdbrain-wiki write, as children of stage 1.
assertions: The size is announced as large before the first question
The outcome names the top-level split as stages in time
Stage 2 is blocked by stage 1 and is not a child of stage 1
The outcome names stage 1's own split as a result split with two children
The outcome is printed only after the interview settles the split
Every question asks exactly one decision as a numbered menu of two or three options, the recommended one first
